notes: IEEE 1516.1-2025 public-API scenario: known candidates publish an owner's attribute; one requests and cancels acquisition while a second receives an assumption callback, and the cancellation confirmation is serviced concurrently. The owner unconditionally divests and the search continues to the canceled candidate. A third published candidate invokes Attribute Ownership Acquisition If Available while the owner still holds the attribute; callback delivery is held until after divestiture, and the test asserts that no Request Attribute Ownership Assumption is invoked at this Willing-to-Acquire candidate, directly covering requirement-candidate-content-clauses-04-federation-management-page-058-l147-40-assumption (§4.12). Other direct mappings are page-148-l61-18 and page-148-l70-21 -> §7.1, p150-l125-39 -> §7.1.2, p153-l129-40 -> §7.1.4, and page-154-l156-49 -> §7.2. The immediate-model path uses standard Disable/Enable Callbacks to hold callbacks until the search boundary. This paired primary/contract case is C++ public-API evidence only, not a conformance claim.
